The science of tests

What can a score tell you?

A psychological test is a measuring tool, and like any tool it needs checking before use. Three key ideas:

  • Reliability: whether it measures consistently. If you take the test again under similar conditions, the result should be similar.
  • Validity: whether it measures what it claims to and suits the intended use. A test can be reliable without being valid.
  • Norms: the group your score is compared with. The same score means different things depending on age, country or test version.

Translating a test is not enough: the new linguistic and cultural version must be shown to work. The International Test Commission's guidelines stress validity, fairness, accessibility and privacy.

That is why Psycholopedia's results describe dimensions with nuance, never ranking people as better or worse or turning a trait into a diagnosis. A short online questionnaire defines no one.
